double_url_encoding.description: Encodes characters twice so that the WAF decodes once and sees safe text, while the application decodes twice and executes the payload. The % character is encoded as %25, converting %3C to %253C.

unicode_normalization.description: Uses Unicode equivalent characters (full-width, overlong UTF-8, or lookalike codepoints) that normalize to ASCII equivalents in the application but are not matched by WAF signatures operating on byte patterns.

html_entity.description: Encodes characters as HTML entities (named, decimal, or hex) that browsers decode before processing but WAFs may not evaluate in the same context. Effective in HTML attribute and JavaScript contexts.

comment_injection.description: Inserts SQL or code comments (/**/, --, #, /*!*/) between keywords and tokens to fragment signatures while keeping the payload syntactically valid. MySQL conditional comments (/*!...*/) are especially powerful as they are executed by MySQL but look like comments to other parsers.

case_variation.description: Alternates upper and lower case letters in keywords to defeat case-sensitive regex patterns. Most SQL databases and JavaScript engines are case-insensitive for keywords and functions.

null_byte.description: Inserts a URL-encoded null byte (%00) to terminate strings early in C-based parsers or to truncate file extensions in older PHP versions, causing the WAF and application to interpret strings differently.

parameter_pollution.description: Sends the same parameter multiple times with different values (HTTP Parameter Pollution, HPP). WAFs may inspect only the first occurrence while the application uses the last, or vice versa, allowing a split payload to bypass detection.

chunked_transfer.description: Uses HTTP chunked transfer encoding to split the request body into chunks. Some WAFs reassemble incorrectly or inspect each chunk independently, allowing payloads split across chunk boundaries to bypass signature matching.
chunked_transfer.example_after:
POST /login with Transfer-Encoding: chunked; body split as '5
admin
3
'--
0
'

http_method_switching.description: Switches the HTTP method (GET→POST, POST→PUT, or using method override headers like X-HTTP-Method-Override) to bypass WAF rules that only apply to specific methods or inspect query strings but not body parameters.
http_method_switching.example_after: POST /search with body: q=<script>alert(1)</script> and header X-HTTP-Method-Override: GET

base64_encoding.description: Wraps the entire payload or parts of it in base64 encoding, which is then decoded by the application (e.g., eval(atob(...)) in JavaScript, base64_decode() in PHP). WAFs matching on plaintext signatures miss the encoded form.

wildcard_obfuscation.description: Uses shell glob wildcards to construct filenames and commands without typing the full string, bypassing keyword-based pattern matching in command injection filters. The shell expands wildcards before execution.

json_unicode_escape.description: Encodes characters within JSON string values as \uXXXX Unicode escape sequences. JSON parsers decode these before the application processes the value, but WAFs scanning raw JSON body bytes may miss the payload.

multipart_boundary_injection.description: Manipulates multipart/form-data boundary strings or field names to confuse WAF parsers that split on boundaries incorrectly, allowing payloads in field values to appear as boundary separators to the WAF but valid data to the server.
multipart_boundary_injection.example_after: Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKit\r\nFormBoundary (with payload injected across the artificial split)

content_type_confusion.description: Sends the payload with an unexpected Content-Type header (e.g., application/json when the WAF expects application/x-www-form-urlencoded) causing the WAF to parse the body differently than the application framework.
content_type_confusion.example_before: POST with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded and body: id=1'
content_type_confusion.example_after: POST with Content-Type: application/json and body: {"id":"1'"}
